bullets.title: NVDA: Leadership vacuum, export controls, and financing tightening dominate narrative
bullets.body: Moody's cut NVDA's credit outlook to stable from positive citing leadership vacuum; board contacted ARM CEO Rene Haas as potential successor to Huang. New BIS export controls require licenses for advanced chips to China, Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil, with TSMC/Samsung halting some shipments. NVDA is tightening vendor financing, reportedly requiring neoclouds to secure customer prepayments for GPU allocations, pressuring CRWV and similar platforms. Jefferies cut PT to $250 on CEO succession concerns; buy-side feedback 'next to zero' with many using NVDA as a short funding vehicle, money rotating into AMD and AVGO.

bullets.title: PANW: Largest beat in 5 years; $4.5B Applied Compute acquisition signals AI-security pivot
bullets.body: F1Q27 revenue $3.44B (+39% YoY) beat Street by ~4%; NGS ARR $9.73B +66% YoY with nnARR +133% YoY. FY27 guidance raised to $14.52-14.57B (+26-27% YoY vs. Street's 23.4%); NGS ARR guidance raised by $400M to $11.475-11.525B. $4.5B all-stock acquisition of Applied Compute targets $1B ARR by FY29 and 100-150MW of compute capacity by FY30, though analysts flag FY28 margin headwinds. Multiple firms raised PTs (Citi to $445 Buy, Piper to $450); stock +10%+ on the day.

bullets.title: BABA: Q2 EPS miss but cloud acceleration at 53% YoY; capex surge and export controls weigh
bullets.body: Q2 revenue CNY271.52B beat consensus; adjusted EBITDA CNY46.06B beat, but non-GAAP EPS CNY8.10 missed CNY10.88 estimate. Cloud revenue grew 53% YoY with AI external revenue +67% YoY; T-Head unveiled Zhenwu V900 chip with mass production Q1 2027. Cloud growth guidance cut to 30-45% for FY27 (from 50%+) due to new compute export controls; capex CNY50.48B (+60% YoY), free cash flow negative CNY34.47B. 2030 target of $100B external cloud revenue with 20%+ margin maintained.

bullets.title: WSM: Q3 EPS beats on tariff refund; Pottery Barn drags comps, stock -5.6% pre-mkt
bullets.body: Q3 EPS $2.38 beat FactSet $2.19; revenue $1.99B slightly missed $2.00B estimate. Comps +5.1% missed by 50bps with Pottery Barn +1.8% the weak link vs. West Elm +7.0%. Q3 benefited from $29.3M tariff refund; FY26 guidance reiterated at 4.7-7.2% revenue growth, 17.8-18.2% operating margin.

bullets.title: GOOGL: +3.9% pre-mkt on Gemini 4 Neon launch; JPM downgrades to Neutral on AI capex concerns
bullets.body: Google launched Gemini 4 Neon AI coding agent at $3/M input tokens and $15/M output tokens with 1M-token context window, scoring 61 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. JPM downgraded Alphabet to Neutral from Overweight as part of a hyperscaler capex/funding gap analysis projecting ~$595B funding shortfall through 2028. GOOGL is cited alongside AMD and AVGO as a potential beneficiary of NVDA's weakening ecosystem position via TPU alternatives.

bullets.title: MDB: UBS upgrades to Buy, $450 PT (47% upside) on durable 20%+ growth
bullets.body: UBS upgraded MongoDB from Neutral to Buy, raising PT to $450 from $375, implying 47% upside from ~$307. Thesis cites durable 20%+ total revenue growth and 25%+ Atlas growth, with no disruption from recent management turnover. Stock +4.0% pre-market.

bullets.title: NET: Tier-1 AI beneficiary; RBC/TIMT conf highlights 10M+ developer base, Act 4 upside
bullets.body: Cloudflare management bullish that Act 4 of its platform could exceed prior acts; Workers developer base crossed 10M. NET added ~5% of total Internet last quarter; GAAP profitability expected in Q4/26. RBC and multiple TIMT conference attendees view NET as a top-tier AI platform play with agentic traffic monetization expanding.

bullets.title: BE: +6.8% pre-mkt on BMO upgrade; MS bus tour highlights multi-project demand shift
bullets.body: Bloom Energy upgraded by BMO Capital driving +6.8% pre-market move. Morgan Stanley SF bus tour found 100+ prospective customers at recent BE customer day, with the company shifting toward multi-project agreements. BE expects Fremont facility possession in 2027 at ~$150M/GW capital cost; identifies CCS and 800V as next growth vectors targeting ~20% service gross margin minimum.

bullets.title: COHR: +8.2% pre-mkt on $2B share repurchase authorization
bullets.body: Coherent announced a $2 billion share repurchase authorization, driving an 8.2% pre-market gain. The optical sector broadly is viewed as poised to rebound with the AI upgrade cycle; MTSI and LITE also among the semi/optical names rallying pre-market (+4.5% and +4.7% respectively).

bullets.title: INTU: Sold off to $313 ahead of tonight's earnings; Mailchimp remains key risk
bullets.body: Intuit dumped from $345 to $313 heading into Q1 earnings tonight (consensus $2.46 EPS, $4.30B revenue). UBS frames setup as likely +13% revenue YoY and $2.60 EPS, with FY27 guidance for 9-10% revenue growth. Mailchimp is flagged as the biggest risk (flat to -1% revenue forecast); software sector sentiment broadly negative on AI displacement fears.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 purchase intent at 5-year high (73%); Duo foldable ranks 3rd in debut
bullets.body: JPM survey shows iPhone 18 purchase intent rose to 73% (vs. 71% in 2025), driven by upgraders (82% of buyers). iPhone Duo ranks third with 14% of selections in its debut year, particularly strong among Android switchers (17%). AI features rank seventh as a purchase driver (~7%), below replacement/performance/camera. JPM maintains Overweight with $360 PT.

bullets.title: HPE/DELL: JPM favors both into earnings on AI server demand; hardware cohort down -20%
bullets.body: JPM flags hardware cohort down -20% avg past month vs. -14% coverage universe, primarily on AI infrastructure concerns. For DELL (reporting Nov 24), JPM expects F3-F4Q27 beat driven by ISG strength; stock trading 10-11x NTM EPS vs. 5-yr avg. For HPE (reporting Nov 23), expects F4Q26 beat and FY27 raise on Cloud & AI revenue growth +60-72% YoY; trading 9-10x NTM EPS. AI server market forecast +90%/+55% in 2026/2027.

bullets.title: MSFT: Ignite signals strong Azure/M365 demand; cost-conscious AI token spending noted
bullets.body: UBS MSFT Ignite and CFO meeting takeaways show strong demand for Azure and M365/Copilot but anecdotal evidence of cost-conscious AI token spending. Anthropic's shift toward applications puts it in direct competition with Microsoft, threatening distribution access per Kedrosky. House China committee separately demanding Microsoft brief on AI cloud deal talks with ByteDance.

bullets.title: AVGO: Positioned to benefit from NVDA weakness via custom silicon; faces land/power headwinds
bullets.body: JPM and GS both flag Broadcom as a key beneficiary of NVDA's weakening ecosystem position via custom silicon exposure for hyperscalers in 2028+. AVGO is cited alongside AMZN as best positioned to benefit from Anthropic IPO success via equity stake and custom silicon demand. However, GS notes AVGO faces headwinds from land/power/shell constraints into FY28 and emerging hyperscaler funding concerns. S&P revised AVGO outlook to Stable from Positive.

bullets.title: EQIX: MS bus tour constructive; 48 retail expansion projects across 32 markets
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley SF bus tour highlights Equinix executing on 48 announced retail expansion projects across 32 markets as of 3Q26, mostly 60MW or less. EQIX is positioning for AI inferencing through dense multi-tenant ecosystems; neoclouds represent less than 2% of monthly recurring revenue. Texas construction remains on schedule; battery supply expected tight in 2027.

bullets.title: AMZN/GOOGL/META/MSFT hyperscalers: JPM flags $595B funding gap 2027-28; mixed ratings
bullets.body: JPM projects $450B AI-related supply for 2027 ($225B hyperscaler issuance + $225B GPU/data center financing), with aggregate FCF negative through 2028 and a ~$595B base-case funding gap. JPM downgrades Alphabet to Neutral, retains Overweight on Amazon and Oracle, Neutral on Meta, Underweight on Microsoft. Despite funding concerns, hyperscalers (META +1.6%, AMZN +2.2%, GOOGL +3.9%) acting well pre-market with no evidence of rotation out to Anthropic IPO.

bullets.title: ALAB: Content per XPU path to $2000+; optical ramp H2/27-28 and CXL H2/27
bullets.body: RBC TIMT conference highlights Astera Labs' path to doubling content per XPU to $2,000+, with optical solutions ramping H2/2027-28 and CXL initial ramp in H2/2027. ALAB also +5.0% pre-market in the broader semi/AI infrastructure complex rally.

bullets.title: INTC: Secures first external customer for 18A advanced chips, foundry milestone
bullets.body: Intel secured its first external customer for 18A advanced chips, a key milestone in its foundry turnaround effort. This is cited across multiple sources (GS, UBS, macro headlines) as a significant positive datapoint for Intel's foundry ambitions, though no rating changes were noted.

bullets.title: SMCI/STX/WDC/MU: Storage and memory complex ripping pre-market on AI sentiment bounce
bullets.body: Storage and memory names surging in pre-market: STX +6.1%, WDC +5.4%, MU +4.6%, SNDK +4.9%. SMCI +3.8%. Sector context: memory GM viewed as near peak with weak confidence in LT supply agreements, but optical and storage poised to rebound with AI upgrade cycle. Nov 18-19 may mark a bottom in AI/semis after a 6-week selloff per sales desk commentary.

bullets.title: TTD: Three senior exec departures amid first revenue decline since 2020
bullets.body: The Trade Desk lost three senior executives—Waseem Basheer, Whitney Rifkin, and Bryce Poll—concurrent with its first revenue decline since 2020. No rating actions noted but cited as a negative signal for the platform's near-term execution.
